security_audit.summary: All 20 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, reference links, placeholder connection text, localhost configuration, or unrelated list text. The review identified two separate medium-severity guidance risks: a broad process termination command and a database example that handles a plaintext password without secure-storage guidance. No prompt injection, malicious network activity, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The troubleshooting workflow terminates every soffice.bin process for the current user.
remediation.suggestion: Replace killall with a targeted process check and require user confirmation before terminating a specific LibreOffice process.

remediation.issue: The external database example assigns a plaintext password and then stores the database document without discussing credential persistence.
remediation.suggestion: Use runtime secret input or an approved credential store, and state whether LibreOffice saves credentials inside the ODB document.

semantic_findings.title: Broad LibreOffice Process Termination
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting example runs killall soffice.bin, which can terminate unrelated LibreOffice sessions and cause loss of unsaved work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command explicitly terminates every matching soffice.bin process. Its broad effect is clear even though the stated intent is socket troubleshooting.

content.value_statement: Database setup and automation across LibreOffice Base can require unfamiliar connection formats and UNO services. This skill provides focused workflows, examples, and operational guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of LibreOffice Base databases in ODB format.
Explains connections for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, JDBC, and ODBC sources.
Provides Python UNO examples for creating database documents and data sources.
Supports planning for tables, queries, forms, reports, imports, and exports.
Provides command-line startup and localhost UNO socket troubleshooting guidance.
limitations: Requires LibreOffice Base and compatible database drivers in the local environment.
Examples use placeholder paths, ports, database names, and credentials that require adaptation.
Does not replace database-specific security, backup, migration, or performance testing.
UNO automation requires a running LibreOffice listener and environment-specific validation.

use_cases.title: Create a Department Database
use_cases.description: Design an ODB database with tables, relationships, forms, and routine reports for a small operational team.

use_cases.title: Connect Base to Existing Data
use_cases.description: Prepare a LibreOffice Base connection to MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, JDBC, or ODBC data sources.

use_cases.title: Automate Report Production
use_cases.description: Plan a Python UNO workflow that opens a database, runs queries, and generates repeatable reports.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a New Base Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a LibreOffice Base database for [purpose]. Include tables, primary keys, relationships, forms, reports, and validation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an External Connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to connect LibreOffice Base to [database type]. Use placeholders and list required drivers, connection fields, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Queries and Reports
prompt_templates.prompt: Design parameterized queries and reports for [business requirement]. Explain indexes, transactions, expected outputs, and test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Create a UNO Automation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a secure Python UNO workflow for [task]. Include listener setup, error handling, secret handling, cleanup, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a customer support database with tickets, customers, agents, and monthly reports.
output: Schema plan covering four related tables with primary and foreign keys.
Form plan for ticket entry and customer lookup.
Report plan for monthly volume, resolution time, and agent workload.

output_examples.input: Help connect LibreOffice Base to an existing PostgreSQL database.
output: Connection field checklist using placeholders for host, port, database, and user.
Validation steps for connectivity, permissions, and a read-only test query.

best_practices: Use parameterized queries, transactions, indexes, and appropriate data types.
Back up databases and test changes against non-production copies.
Keep credentials outside prompts, scripts, connection documents, and version control.
anti_patterns: Do not place real passwords or production connection details in generated examples.
Do not terminate all LibreOffice processes without checking active work and receiving confirmation.
Do not apply placeholder commands or connection strings without environment-specific validation.

faq.question: What database formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers ODB workflows and connections for embedded databases, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, JDBC, and ODBC sources.

faq.question: Does this skill install LibreOffice or database drivers?
faq.answer: No. It can explain prerequisites and installation commands, but users must approve and perform environment changes.

faq.question: Can it create forms and reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan forms, reports, templates, queries, and automation workflows for LibreOffice Base.

faq.question: Does Python automation require UNO?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented Python workflows require LibreOffice UNO and a reachable local listener.

faq.question: Can I use production database credentials?
faq.answer: Use placeholders during planning. Provide secrets only through an approved runtime secret mechanism, never through prompts or stored examples.

faq.question: Will generated workflows work without testing?
faq.answer: No. Driver versions, permissions, paths, schemas, and LibreOffice configuration require local validation before production use.
